strategy_summary: Person-driven. Resolve scalar codes (actress role_id, [jp] country_code). Build cn_jp bitset over company_name rows. Scan name for LIKE '%Yo%' AND NOT '%Yu%' to get candidate pids (~20,911). For each pid walk cast_info__person_id CSR, filter role_id==actress AND note=='(voice: English version)' (~394 surviving rows). For each surviving (pid, movie_id): walk movie_companies__movie_id offsets, apply mc.note LIKE %(Japan)% AND NOT %(USA)%, check cn_jp bitset on mc.company_id-1. If passes, also require aka_name exists for pid (offsets_only). Update running MIN over aka_name.name in pid's aka_name range and MIN(title.title) at row mv-1.

join_order.notes: Use CSR per pid; ~151,718 ci rows visited total.
Walk per-movie mc range; apply LIKE filters and cn_jp bitset check.
Precomputed bitset: cn.country_code == '[jp]' → set bit at cn_row.
Semi-join: pid must have aka_name rows. Also iterate that range to MIN aka_name.name.

filters.predicate: name LIKE '%Yo%' AND name NOT LIKE '%Yu%'
role_id = actress_id AND note = '(voice: English version)'
note LIKE '%(Japan)%' AND note NOT LIKE '%(USA)%'

data_structures.ci_walk: no materialization; iterate CSR rowids and filter inline
data_structures.aggregation: two std::string running-min buffers under a mutex (or per-thread + final reduce)

morsel_phases.output: thread-local vector<int32_t> pids, concatenated at end

min_strategy: Per-thread (min_an_name, min_title) as std::string; on update copy shorter-lex string. Final reduction picks lexicographic min across threads. MIN(an1.name) ranges over all aka_name rows in pid's range that pass all join conditions (per query semantics, every (pid,mv) row that passes contributes all matching an1 rows).

memory_estimate_mb.mmap_columns: OS-managed (cast_info ~145MB role_id + 145MB person_id index rowids etc.)
